blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: []{#sec:intro label="sec:intro"} The finite logarithm was introduced by Kontsevich (under the name "The $1\frac{1}{2}$ logarithm") in [@Kon99]. The finite logarithm is the case $n=1$ of the $n$-th polylogarithm $\operatorname{li}_n\in \mathbb{Z}/p[z]$ defined by $\operatorname{li}_n(z)= \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} z^k/k^n$. In loc. cit. Kontsevich proved that the finite logarithm satisfies a 4-term functional equation, known as the fundamental equation of information theory. blocks.content:
[]{#sec:proof label="sec:proof"}

The connection between $p$-adic and finite polylogarithms is made by the following

::: proposition
Let $\operatorname{Li}^{(p)}_n(z):= \operatorname{Li}_n(z)- \operatorname{Li}_n(z^p)/p^n$. Then $\operatorname{Li}^{(p)}_n(X) \subset
  W$ and the function $\operatorname{Li}^{(p)}_n$ reduces modulo $p$ to $(1-z^p)^{-1}
  \operatorname{li}_n(z)$.
:::

blocks.title: Another proof of the main result
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:another label="sec:another"}

In this section we sketch another proof of the main result. This proof has two interesting features: First of all, it proves directly the formula for $F_n$ in terms of the functions $L_n(z)$ defined at the end of the last section. This formula is of course simpler than the original formula. The other feature is that the key ingredient in the proof is a formula, discovered by Rob de Jeu and the author, which seems to be of some further importance.
